title: Triangle Savings Initiative: cadence & rollout plan for batching, caching, quantization
creator: Alina Park
description: Initiative-level tracker and rollout plan for coordinated experiments that combine batching, KV/prefix caching, and lightweight quantization profiles to reduce per-token cost across production workloads. The goal is to define a repeatable cadence (hypothesis -> field trial -> evaluation -> rollout) and a safety scaffold to prevent regressions in latency and quality. This doc captures milestones, owners, required infra work, and decision thresholds for scaling each knob from pilot to platform-wide opt-in.
objectives: Reduce average hosted per-token cost by 18% on conversational workloads within Q2 2026
Establish a standardized validation pipeline for quality/regression checks tied to each experiment
Create an operational rollout pattern that allows 1% -> 10% -> 50% traffic ramp with automated rollback criteria
acceptance_criteria: Field trials instrumented with token-level cost and latency probes across 3 representative customer segments
Automated quality checks (WER/semantic-similarity + promptset baselines) pass at configured thresholds for candidate quant profiles
Runbook and A/B configuration available in Console for canary traffic splits and immediate fallback to baseline model variants
deliverables: Experiment scaffold template (Runbook + dashboard naming convention)
Three pilot experiments: short-chat Batching+, long-chat Prefetch+KV, embeddings-optimized quant profile
Consolidated rollup dashboard and automated alerting for regression signals
milestones: 2026-02-25: Initiative kickoff and baseline metric collection
2026-03-05: Infra tickets created for canaries and metric tagging (ENG-23456)
2026-04-07: Quant profile bench and human eval batch complete
2026-04-20: Decision gate for 10% ramp: cost vs. quality tradeoffs documented
2026-04-30: Target release window for first cohort of rollouts
risks: Quality regressions for rare prompt patterns when using aggressive quantization
Increased p95 latency if batching heuristics misalign with customer latency SLOs
Metrics noise from multi-tenant mixing could obscure signal — requires segmented telemetry
mitigations: Hold back high-risk customers behind ‘conservative’ profile; require explicit opt-in for aggressive profiles
Introduce adaptive batching caps for latency-sensitive routes; route-level overrides in Console
Segmented analysis dashboard and bootstrapped significance tests for regression alerting
comments: 2026-02-26: PM sync — agreed to split pilots by workload archetype; added ENG-19843 for logging instrumentation. — Alina
2026-03-03: Eng update — batching prototype landed, but p95 increased on one customer workload; added adaptive cap A/B. — Mateo
2026-03-08: Design review — Console exposure for rollouts should use existing route-level controls; mockups uploaded to Drive. — Priya Shah (Design)
2026-03-12: Pilot 1 live at 1%. Early signal: token cost -6% on short-chat; no quality regression on sampled prompts. Continue 1% for one week. — Mateo

decisions: Use a three-stage rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with automated rollback at predefined thresholds
Adopt lightweight int8 quant profiles as default ‘conservative’ option; keep int4 behind opt-in for specific customers
Prioritize batching heuristics adjustments for latency-insensitive routes first
